transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess what brings me in is that I just can’t seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I try to work, and it’s like one saw starting up, or someone walking past the office, or even just a thought about another job, and I’m pulled off what I was doing. Then somehow the whole day gets away from me. I don’t know if that makes sense, but it’s been… more than I can really manage lately.
Has this trouble concentrating been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a new change for you recently?

I think it’s been there a long time, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad student or anything—I wasn’t trying to be careless—but even in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my mother I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, forget instructions, or just kind of stare out the window instead of finishing my work. So… I guess it’s not exactly new.
Do you find yourself frequently worrying about various things—like health, work, or family—more days than not, even when there's no clear reason to worry?

I’m not sure I’d call it worrying like that, exactly. I mean, I think about work and family the way anyone would, I guess, but I don’t know that I’m sitting around worrying more days than not for no reason. At least… I haven’t noticed it that way. Does that answer what you mean?
Over the past two weeks or so, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy, most of the day nearly every day?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, when I can’t get things done, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been down most of the day nearly every day. And I still care about the things I normally like. I think it’s more… the focus problem than feeling sad, if that’s okay to say.
Does this trouble with focus and distractibility cause noticeable problems for you in more than one area of life—like both at work and at home or in relationships—not just one?

Yes… I think it does, unfortunately. I try not to make excuses for it, but at work it’s caused real problems. I’ve made mistakes or been late getting things done, and that’s cost me commissions or meant redoing parts of jobs. The crew doesn’t really depend on me as much now for scheduling or ordering because I’ll miss something.

And at home, too… my husband has kind of had to take over the bills and reminders because I misplace papers or forget what needs doing. I hate saying that, but yes, it’s more than just one area.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting or speaking impulsively without thinking it through?

A little, yes… I don’t think I’m impulsive so much, or at least I try not to be. But if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or sit through a long meeting, I get this wound-up feeling inside, like I need to get up and move around. Even when there’s no real reason—I mean, my wrist is healed now, and I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish. I can do it, but it feels harder than it probably should.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with chronic, longstanding inattention (distractibility, forgetfulness, losing items, careless errors) dating back to before age 12, confirmed by childhood teacher reports. Symptoms cause impairment in multiple domains (work performance, home responsibilities/relationship). Mild hyperactive/restless symptoms (inner restlessness, need to move) are also present but secondary to the inattentive symptoms. Anxiety (GAD) and depressive disorder were explicitly screened for and denied, ruling out F41.1 and F32.9 as primary diagnoses.
